findings: TOP BOTTLENECK: 'first review → last push' (active/rework) stage. Median 2.7h overall, but the slowest 12% of PRs (7/60) each take >48h — dominated by a 67h median rework window. These 7 PRs collectively drove P90 to 55.5h.

ROOT CAUSE: Branch contamination + CI conflict coordination deadlock. Measured (not assumed): 8/11 PRs in a coordination group carried contaminated CI-file diffs (squash-merge relands under new SHAs). The group serialized 18 PRs for up to 64h while head-of-line PR #1976 (28/30 commits patch-identical to main) could not move. Emergency fix PR #2168 (coordination default-off) landed 2026-07-28 and drained the blockage.

SECONDARY ROOT CAUSE: Model-unavailability CI-recovery stalls. PR #2003 had a 70h gap where CI recovery was attempting to dispatch but the model was unavailable; the sweep retried on the same broken model instead of backing off. The new dispatch observability (PR #2129) will make future stalls diagnosable in seconds.

Guard friction is low and catch-correct. pr-preflight and pr-review-ledger each have 5 denies / 155 events (3.2%) — all verified as genuine policy violations, not mis-fires. authoring-main-sync: 2,757 allows / 0 denies — nominal.
Apple estimation is excellent: 89% exact, median |error| = 0.0 🍎 across 557 sessions. No systematic under-estimation.
PROPOSED SMALLEST FIX (see below): Add cherry-based contamination detection to the CI conflict coordinator so that the coordination fence can be safely re-enabled without deadlocking innocent PRs.

proposedFix.title: Cherry-based contamination detection in CI conflict coordinator
proposedFix.currentBehavior: isCiCoordinationPath() flags a PR as touching CI files if ANY diff file matches the path pattern. Branch contamination (squash-merge carries prior-session commits under new SHAs) causes innocent art/docs PRs to match, creating false-positive coordination groups.
proposedFix.proposedChange: Before adding a PR to a coordination group, run `git cherry -v origin/main <branch-head>` (or equivalent via GitHub Commits API) to count genuinely NEW commits (marked '+') that touch CI paths. A PR with 0 new CI-touching commits is contaminated and should be excluded from the coordination group (or labelled for passive observation only, not blocking).
proposedFix.measurability: Contamination rate: PRs in coordination groups with 0 genuine CI-path changes / total PRs in group. Before fix: ~73% (8/11 measured 2026-07-28). After fix: target 0%. Would allow CI_CONFLICT_COORDINATION_ENFORCE to be re-enabled safely.
proposedFix.scope: Tooling-only — no gameplay or runtime change. Cap: 3🍎 per tooling-only ceiling.
proposedFix.effort: 2–3🍎 estimated. Requires: (1) a cherry-check helper, (2) coordinator integration, (3) unit tests with real-git fixtures, (4) a contamination-rate metric reported in the CI-health canvas.
alternativesConsidered: Keep coordination default-off permanently — accepted risk: when re-enabled for any reason, the false-positive problem recurs silently.
Rebase all agent branches before grouping — heavier (requires write access per PR), still doesn't prevent new contamination on long-lived PRs.
Filter by commit count (skip PRs with >50% patch-identical commits) — proxy only; `git cherry` is authoritative and not significantly more expensive.
